title: Rally Saturday in N.D.G. for Black man killed in intervention by Montreal police
article: Montreal groups protesting police violence and systemic racism are staging a demonstration on Saturday to mark the death of Sheffield Matthews, who was killed in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce during a police intervention.

The demonstration will begin at 2 p.m. at Trenholme Park in N.D.G. It will be followed by a placing of flowers at the spot where he was fatally shot by police, on Côte-St-Luc Rd. near West Hill Ave. It's being organized by Black Lives Matter Montreal and the Defund the Police Coalition.

According to a report by Quebec's Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes that is investigating the case, on Oct. 29, police responded to a 911 call of a man in crisis at around 6 a.m. Police said Matthews was holding a knife and approached their car, then walked toward a vehicle in which a civilian was sitting. When police tried to intervene, they said Matthews lunged at them with the knife, and they fatally shot him.

"This is yet another case of someone from our community dying at the hands of the police and it's another case of police intervening in a case where there was someone in distress, someone with a mental health crisis," said Marlihan Lopez, an organizer with Black Lives Matter Montreal." It's another example of how police are not equipped and should not be responding to mental health crises."
The shooting furthers the argument for defunding the police force and putting more money toward intervention teams who are trained to intervene in health care crises, Lopez said.

Côte-des-Neiges-Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough mayor Sue Montgomery said she plans to attend the event. Shortly after the incident, Montgomery issued a statement saying the shooting was a reminder of the borough's "sad and tragic" history of police violence against Black men.

In 1987, Anthony Griffin, 19 and unarmed, was shot and killed by police after a complaint he had not paid his taxi fare. Nicholas Gibbs, 23, was fatally shot in 2018 after allegedly threatening police with a knife. Members of Gibbs' family will be at the demonstration Saturday.

"The senseless killing of people of colour needs to end," Montgomery wrote. "Systemic racism is undeniable. It is present in the SPVM and in all facets of our society. ... We need police trained to help people in crisis, not kill them."
Her comments were condemned by Montreal police union president Yves Francoeur as "totally irresponsible."

Sabrina Holland, who described herself as a close family friend, said in a video posted to Facebook that Matthews was a gentle person who worked in an old-age home caring for seniors and spent most of his earnings on his family, CTV News reported. She said he struggled with poverty, but his alleged crisis was unusual for him, and he was not violent.

Alfred Dear, president of the St. Vincent and the Grenadines Association of Montreal, said on Friday that Matthews's sister had contacted him to seek information on how to come to Canada to organize his burial. She lives in New York, as does Matthews's mother, and the coronavirus pandemic is making it difficult for them to enter Canada. The family is originally from St. Vincent and the Grenadines.
